title: reMaestro featured plugins
description: The one file at curation/featured.json: which plugins the console puts in front of somebody browsing, and in what order. Written by a maintainer and never by a publisher — the same authority the verified tier has, for a related but different reason. A tier is EVIDENTIAL: it records something that was checked, and it is refused unless the evidence resolves at a derived URL. Featuring is EDITORIAL: nobody checked anything, somebody decided. Neither may be written by its subject, and nothing here may be read as either a tier or a safety claim; see README.md.

updatedAt.description: When somebody last decided this. A date rather than a timestamp: an editorial list changes on the scale of weeks.

spotlight.description: At most one plugin, with a sentence about why. Its own field rather than the first row of the list because it carries prose a maintainer wrote about somebody else's software, which is a heavier thing to publish than a place in an order — so the blurb is required, and you cannot spotlight something without saying why. A plugin may be spotlit or featured and never both; the validator refuses the overlap rather than resolving it.

plugin.description: The id of a plugin with a directory in plugins/. Refused if there is none, and refused if it has no version anybody could install.

blurb.description: Why this one, in a sentence somebody reading the store would find useful. It is our editorial voice about a stranger's binary, so it may describe what a plugin does and must never say or imply that it is safe, audited or endorsed — nothing here checked any of that.

featured.description: An ordered list. The order IS the editorial content, which is why this is one file rather than a record per plugin: a reordering has to read as a reordering in a diff, and two records each carrying a rank would collide with no conflict.

note.description: For whoever reads this file in a year — why this is on the list. Not published: the index carries the order and the spotlight's blurb and nothing else, because a note per row is a second place for our voice to end up beside a stranger's plugin without anybody having reviewed it as copy.
